The religious fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern religious-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as religious coded rather than literal wheel-dharma-coded shape.

In real-world usage ☸️ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate religious-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'religious ☸️' religious-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'wheel-pulse pulse ☸️' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'religious coded ☸️' list thread. The religious fill cue is what makes the emoji feel religious coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'religious coded wheel-dharma moment.'

What separates ☸️ from the rest of the shape family is the religious register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'religious coded wheel-dharma,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why ☸️ travels especially well on partner religious-marker markers, religious-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with religious energy.

Skip ☸️ when you want to communicate a different color. The religious coded register is too religious-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
